observation.visible_scene: A dark stage with a glowing neon-style set: at the center stands a DJ console/booth outlined in orange-yellow, showing two green turntable tops and four red speaker circles arranged 2x2. Around it are humanoid dancers rendered as glowing LED outlines wearing fedora hats with red glowing 'eyes' and red/blue shoes. For most of the excerpt there are three dancers (left, center behind the booth, right); near the end additional dancers appear at the edges.
visible_changes: The dancers perform a continuous, mirrored stepping/leaning routine: side dancers lift a knee, lean their torso back, swing bent arms, and periodically thrust both arms forward to point, while the center dancer gestures over the console, spreading and drawing in its arms and pointing outward.

The center and side figures keep roughly the same horizontal positions throughout (left inner dancer ~x320, center ~x510, right inner ~x665), so the motion is body choreography rather than translation across the stage.
The speaker-circle outlines on the booth pulse between red and green/yellow across frames, an independent lighting effect on the static prop.

Around t≈2.27 s the dancers' neon outline color shifts from teal/green to purple/magenta, and two larger purple-outlined dancers become visible at the far left (~x150) and far right (~x850), expanding the visible group from three to five while the booth stays fixed in size and position.
The overall camera framing of the booth appears unchanged (no obvious pan/zoom), so the new edge dancers and color shift read as a scene/segment change rather than continuous camera motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: The choreography before t=0 and after the last frame is not shown; the excerpt begins and ends mid-routine.
What causes the color change and the appearance of the extra edge dancers (a cut, a lighting cue, or dancers entering) is not visible.
Whether the black background and booth are exactly static or subject to minor unseen camera drift is not determinable.
uncertain_details: Whether the extra side dancers are newly revealed by a wider framing or are different performers entering the shot.
The precise reason for the teal-to-purple neon recoloring.
Exact timing of the transition point (between the t=2.20 and t=2.27 samples).
